title: Sweetening Agents Including Honey

official_sources.title: Chapter 2.8 — Sweetening Agents Including Honey, Version 1 (01.09.2023)
Advisory dated 07.11.2025 — HMF to be considered a quality parameter in Honey
FoSCoS Guidance Document — Bees Wax under Category 99

regulatory_notes: The active consolidated Chapter 2.8 is Version 1 dated 01.09.2023.

A 2024 draft proposed a new 2.8.13 standard for High Fructose Corn Syrup. It is not present in the current consolidated Chapter 2.8 and is therefore not treated as an operative Chapter 2.8 product standard in PMSV.
FSSAI advisory dated 07.11.2025 clarifies that Honey exceeding the 80 mg/kg HMF limit is to be categorised as Substandard; the 80 mg/kg numerical limit itself remains unchanged.

common_rules.text: Food additives are permitted only where allowed by the relevant Chapter 2.8 standard and Appendix A. Honey under 2.8.3(1) explicitly permits no added food ingredient or food additive.
Applicable products must comply with the Food Safety and Standards (Contaminants, Toxins and Residues) Regulations.
Appendix B microbiological requirements apply where expressly referenced by the product standard.

Current Food Safety and Standards (Labelling and Display) Regulations, 2020 apply in addition to product-specific declarations. Historical references in the consolidated chapter to the former Packaging and Labelling Regulations, 2011 are not treated as the current labelling instrument.

standards.name: Honey
standards.definition: Natural sweet substance produced by honey bees from nectar, secretions of living plant parts or excretions of plant-sucking insects, collected and transformed by bees and left in honeycomb to ripen and mature.
variants: Blend of Honeydew and Blossom Honey

composition.parameter: Total reducing sugars — Carvia callosa and Honeydew honey
Total reducing sugars — blend of Honeydew with blossom honey
Sucrose — Carvia callosa and Honeydew honey

composition.enforcement_note: FSSAI advisory 07.11.2025: exceedance is categorised as Substandard; HMF is treated as a quality parameter.

advisory_source.finding: HMF non-compliance is Substandard; no inference about other safety parameters.

mrpl.meaning: minimum required method performance; NOT a permissible concentration

composition.evaluation_note: Absence must be evaluated with method capability and the actual result; no concentration allowance is created by the MRPL.

process_rules: Honey shall not be heated or processed to an extent that changes its essential composition or impairs its quality.
label_rules: Use Honeydew Honey, Blend of Honeydew Honey and Blossom Honey, or Carvia Callosa Honey where the applicable definition is met.
Honey obtained by pressing broodless combs shall include the applicable Pressed Honey designation.
Monofloral Honey requires pollen from the named plant species to be at least 45% of total pollen.
Multi Floral Honey applies where no plant species exceeds 45% of total pollen.
The Chapter 2.8 honey standards apply to packaged/processed honey.
interpretation_notes: Origin, pressed extraction and floral labelling are separate dimensions. A missing origin must not default to general honey for conditional rows.
The printed monofloral >=45% and multifloral <=45% pollen definitions overlap at exactly 45%; no exclusive-label inference is made here.
